rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Blood minerals and memory: the Great Lakes in focus
rfi.description: This week, Spotlight on Africa turns to the Great Lakes region. First, a new Global Witness report reveals how coltan is being smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, amid the ongoing conflict in the east, through Rwanda and on to companies worldwide. Then, artist Grada Kilomba discusses her journey to create a unique monument for Paris commemorating the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'Export trade has increased since exiting the EU, it's been a win'
rfi.description: Ten years after the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains one of the most contested political decisions in recent British history. Its legacy is increasingly shaped by diverging interpretations of sovereignty and the UK's place in the world. RFI spoke to Brexit supporter Robert Oulds, director of British think tank the Bruges Group, about what has changed.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: the promises, the costs and the search for accountability
rfi.description: Ten years on, the UK's decision to leave the European Union is increasingly seen as more than a single referendum result. Critics argue it reflected a wider crisis of political imagination, with Brexit supporters misreading both Britain and the world, while the promised future never arrived.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch will be inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the Republic’s most symbolic ceremonies.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages

rfi.title: Messi notches up World Cup goals record to take Argentina into knockout stages

rfi.title: Haaland scores twice as Norway outwit Senegal to reach last 32 at World Cup
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice on Monday night as Norway advanced to the knockout stages at the World Cup following a pulsating 3-2 victory over Senegal in New Jersey.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

rfi.title: France's scorching weekend heat leads to elderly deaths and spate of drownings
rfi.description: The deaths of three elderly people in southwestern France have been linked to the heatwave hitting the country, while authorities have reported an increase in drownings, as people seek relief from the heat in rivers and lakes.

rfi.title: UK's Starmer resigns as prime minister
rfi.description: UK leader Keir Starmer announced his resignation on Monday following months of pressure, kickstarting a process that will see Britain get its seventh prime minister in a decade.

rfi.title: DRC announces free healthcare for all illnesses in Ituri as Ebola gains ground
rfi.description: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced the introduction of free healthcare for all diseases in Ituri – a pilot project that authorities hope to extend nationwide. lemonde.description: Fortement dépendant des hydrocarbures du Golfe, Pékin est toutefois parvenu à réduire sa consommation d’or noir depuis les tensions autour du détroit d’Ormuz. lemonde.title: Les déboires d’Ilia Traber, le mafieux de Saint-Pétersbourg qui doit beaucoup à Vladimir Poutine

zeit.title: Cindy Cohn: »Ja, manche Kämpfe gewinnen momentan leider die Bösen«
zeit.description: Seit 30 Jahren kämpft Cindy Cohn für digitale Verschlüsselung und gegen Überwachung. Ist in Trumps Amerika noch etwas übrig von den Verheißungen des freien Internets?

zeit.title: Zuwanderung und Wachstum in der Schweiz: 10 Ideen für 10 Millionen
zeit.description: Die Schweiz braucht einen Plan, wie sie mit ihrem Erfolg und ihrem Wohlstand umgehen soll. So könnte er aussehen.

zeit.title: Tag der Industrie: Merz will den »Wohlstand für die Jugend«
zeit.description: Kanzler Friedrich Merz feiert den Bericht der Rentenkommission. Doch die Industrie empfängt ihn beim Jahrestreff mit harter Kritik. Dann überrascht er mit einer Vision.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: 11.000 Seeleute sollen durch die Straße von Hormus evakuiert werden
zeit.description: Die UN-Schifffahrtsorganisation will 11.000 festsitzende Seeleute aus der Golfregion evakuieren. Israel greift weiter im Libanon an. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Fall Ulmen Fernandes: Oberlandesgericht untersagt weitere Teile der Ulmen-Berichterstattung
zeit.description: Der »Spiegel« muss seine Berichterstattung zum Fall Ulmen Fernandes anpassen. Ein Gericht verbietet, den Verdacht zu erwecken, Ulmen könnte Deepfakes verbreitet haben.

france24fr.title: Canicule : la France connaît sa journée la plus chaude jamais enregistrée
france24fr.description: Mardi a été la journée "la plus chaude enregistrée en France" depuis le début des mesures en 1947, alors que de nombreux records absolus de température ont été battus dans l'ouest du pays, a indiqué Météo-France.

france24fr.title: J.D. Vance a-t-il été snobé par le Premier ministre qatari ?
france24fr.description: Sur les réseaux sociaux, une séquence tournée à Genève alimente des interprétations selon lesquelles le vice-président américain aurait été ignoré par le Premier ministre qatari. Mais les images ne racontent pas toute l’histoire.

france24fr.title: Comment Donald Trump s’est pris les pieds dans le bassin réfléchissant de Washington
france24fr.description: Le chantier de l'épuration de l'eau du célèbre bassin réfléchissant au pied du Lincoln Memorial à Washington est en train de tourner au cauchemar politique pour Donald Trump, qui s'y est personnellement investi. C'est une remise en cause de ses compétences premières : celles d'un magnat de l’immobilier censé savoir construire “une piscine”.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : Tulsi Gabbard sous l'emprise d'une secte ? Les révélations du Washington Post
france24fr.description: L’ancienne cheffe du renseignement, Tulsi Gabbard, aurait-elle été influencée par une secte ? C'est ce qu'affirme une enquête publiée par le Washington Post. Les explications de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: Les Fausses Notes du Brexit
france24fr.description:
Dix ans après le référendum qui a bouleversé le Royaume-Uni, quel est l'impact du Brexit sur l'une de ses plus grandes richesses : sa musique ?
 
De Liverpool à Paris, Sonia Patricelli part à la rencontre de celles et ceux qui font vivre la scène musicale britannique. Artistes confirmés, groupes émergents, producteurs et organisateurs de festivals racontent comment la sortie de l'Union européenne a transformé leur quotidien : tournées plus coûteuses, démarches administratives interminables, disp

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : la tour Eiffel ferme plus tôt que prévu
france24fr.description: La tour Eiffel a fermé ce mardi dès 16H00 et le musée du Louvre fera de même de mercredi jusqu'à samedi en raison de la canicule, ont annoncé leurs directions.

france24fr.title: Côte d'Ivoire : le gouvernement veut ouvrir une nouvelle ère dans l'organisation des élections
france24fr.description: En l’absence d’échéances électorales immédiates, la Côte d’Ivoire prend le temps de la réflexion. Quel système électoral construire pour l’avenir ? Après la dissolution de la Commission électorale indépendante, critiquée lors du dernier scrutin, la classe politique planche désormais sur une nouvelle architecture. Une concertation a été lancée ce lundi 22 juin à Abidjan, où le Premier ministre a reçu opposition et société civile pour esquisser les contours d’une réforme visant à restaurer transpa

france24fr.title: Oman et l'Iran vont étudier les coûts de la future gestion du détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: Réaffirmant leur "engagement à maintenir un passage sécurisé à travers le détroit" d'Ormuz et soulignant leur souveraineté sur cette voie maritime stratégique, Oman et l'Iran se sont engagés mardi à se pencher sur les coûts de la future gestion du détroit verrouillé par Téhéran pendant la guerre.

france24fr.title: Entrée de Marc Bloch au Panthéon : un historien, combattant et résistant mort pour la France
france24fr.description: L'historien Marc Bloch, soldat et résistant assassiné par la Gestapo, entre mardi au Panthéon lors d'un hommage à l'auteur de "L'Etrange défaite", ouvrage majeur sur la débâcle de 1940 considéré par Emmanuel Macron comme un avertissement contre le "conformisme" qui sape la "volonté française". Les précisions de Denis Peschanski, historien au CNRS, spécialiste de la Seconde Guerre mondiale.

france24fr.title: Souveraineté dans la cybersécurité : le tournant européen ?
france24fr.description: Aux avant-postes est à Vivatech, grand rendez-vous des startups, pour une émission exceptionnelle sur la souveraineté numérique. Pour en parler, Ali Laïdi reçoit Athénaïs Oslati, PDG de ONTBO, Frédéric Saffroy, associé chez Alerion Avocats, Louis Vildé, président de l'AFIAS, alliance française dans le secteur de l'IA, et Philippe Notton, PDG de Sipearl.

france24fr.title: Marc Bloch au Panthéon : une BD retrace le parcours de l'historien, membre de la Résistance
france24fr.description: L'historien Marc Bloch, soldat et résistant assassiné par la Gestapo, entre mardi au Panthéon lors d'un hommage à l'auteur de "L'Etrange défaite", ouvrage majeur sur la débâcle de 1940 considéré par Emmanuel Macron comme un avertissement contre le "conformisme" qui sape la "volonté française". Les précisions de

france24fr.title: "Des dégâts considérables" : dix ans après, le Brexit continue de plomber l'économie britannique
france24fr.description: Une décennie s'est écoulée depuis le Brexit et les chiffres sont sans appel : la sortie de l'Union européenne a réduit le PIB britannique de 8 %. Tandis que les experts anticipent des conséquences durables, près de 60 % des Britanniques estiment aujourd'hui que quitter l'UE était une erreur.

france24fr.title: Iran – États-Unis : dans le Golfe, la méfiance persiste malgré la reprise du dialogue
france24fr.description: Le lancement des négociations entre Washington et Téhéran en Suisse a ravivé l’espoir d’une désescalade régionale. Mais les monarchies du Golfe, directement exposées à une éventuelle riposte iranienne, se méfient du mémorandum signé par l’administration Trump, jugé "trop favorable" à Téhéran. Il suscite davantage d’inquiétudes que de soulagement au sujet du détroit d’Ormuz, de la question nucléaire ou des missiles iraniens.

france24fr.title: Albanie : 24e jour de manifestations à Tirana contre un projet immobilier lié à Trump
france24fr.description: Des milliers d'Albanais se sont rassemblés vendredi 19 juin à Tirana pour le 20e jour consécutif pour s'opposer à un projet de complexe touristique de luxe lié à la fille de Donald Trump, Ivanka, et son mari Jared Kushner.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'emblématique "Lumumba Vea" est arrivé de RD Congo
france24fr.description:
L'emblématique Michel Kuka Mboladinga, dit "Lumumba Vea", est enfin arrivé au Mondial 2026. Le supporter n'avait pas pu assister au premier match de la RD Congo en raison d'une quarantaine obligatoire liée à Ebola.
 
Lumumba Vea s'était fait connaître à la Coupe d'Afrique des Nations en incarnant, immobile, le héros de l'indépendance congolaise Patrice Lumumba.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : La France en 16èmes, le Sénégal mal en points, l'Algérie se reprend
france24fr.description:
La France, l'Argentine et la Norvège ont décroché lundi leur billet pour les 16es de finale du Mondial, à nouveau portées par le talent de Kylian Mbappé, Lionel Messi et Erling Haaland, tous auteurs d'un doublé. 
 
L'Algérie redresse la barre face à la Jordanie (2-1) et jouera sa place en 16èmes de finale face à l'Autriche samedi. Le Sénégal devra lui, l'emporter largement face à l'Irak pour espérer poursuivre sa route.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : records de chaleur et nuits tropicales, le pays à rude épreuve
france24fr.description: Après des records de température lundi et la nuit la plus chaude jamais enregistrée en France depuis 1947, la canicule exceptionnelle qui frappe le pays s'étend encore mardi, mettant les infrastructures et les organismes à rude épreuve avec des pics attendus à 44°C dans le sud-ouest. Les explications de Gaël Musquet, météorologue, spécialiste de la prévention des catastrophes naturelles.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : après le déluge, la France au rendez-vous des 16e
france24fr.description: Les joueurs de l'équipe de France ont tenté de "rester concentrés" pendant "l'interminable" attente de plus de deux heures due à des risques d'orage entre les deux périodes de leur victoire face à l'Irak 3-0 lundi à Philadelphie.

nzz.title: Wer ist der Beste, Messi oder Mbappé? Zwei Superstars kämpfen um die WM-Torjägerkrone
nzz.description: Die Weltmeisterschaft wird zum Generationenduell. Lionel Messi bricht den WM-Torrekord, doch Kylian Mbappé jagt ihn – die Zeit spielt für den Franzosen.

nzz.title: Versteckspiel um Taliban-Besuch bei der EU: Ohne Gegenleistungen wollen die Islamisten nicht über Ausschaffungen reden
nzz.description: Unter grosser Geheimhaltung sind Vertreter der afghanischen De-facto-Regierung nach Brüssel gereist. Die EU-Staaten sind auf ihre Mitarbeit angewiesen, wollen sie aber nicht diplomatisch anerkennen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Tag der Entscheidung der Zürcher FDP: Wen schicken die Freisinnigen ins Rennen um den Regierungsrat?
nzz.description: Am Dienstagabend bittet die Partei zur Delegiertenversammlung in Zürich. Das wichtigste Traktandum des Abends: die Kandidatenkür für die Wahl in die Kantonsregierung 2027. Die NZZ berichtet live.

nzz.title: Zweifel an Unabhängigkeit und Unparteilichkeit: Das Bundesgericht setzt die Genfer Staatsanwaltschaft in einem Betrugsfall in den Ausstand
nzz.description: Die höchsten Richter haben der Verteidigung recht gegeben. Denn es geht um den Vater des Generalstaatsanwalts Olivier Jornot.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Vertreter aus Libanon und Israel verhandeln erneut in den USA +++ Zulassungszahlen zur Strasse von Hormuz könnten täglich variieren
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Frische Idee für die Steuern: Überschüsse gehören den Bürgern
nzz.description: Der Kampf gegen die Steuer- und Abgabenlast ist ein urliberales Anliegen. Es ist erfreulich, dass die FDP das erkannt hat.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Nicht reden, sondern umsetzen: Die Rentenreform liefert die Chance, die Stimmung im Land zu drehen
nzz.description: Die Gremium hat geliefert, woran Vorgängerregierungen jahrzehntelang gescheitert sind. Kanzler Friedrich Merz könnte sich nun als echter Reformer profilieren – wenn er die nötige Durchsetzungskraft besitzt.

nzz.title: 15-Jähriger ertrinkt in der Limmat, ein Kollege filmt den Sprung und alarmiert die Polizei erst nach 27 Minuten
nzz.description: Ein 20-jähriger Angolaner steht wegen Unterlassung der Nothilfe vor dem Bezirksgericht Zürich. Die Staatsanwältin verlangt sechs Monate Freiheitsstrafe.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: SpaceX-Aktie stabilisiert sich nach Kursrutsch
Nach dem Sportchef ist im EV Zug nun auch der CEO Geschichte – der Klub zerfleischt sich unter dem Präsidenten Hans-Peter Strebel selbst
nzz.description: Zerstritten, konzeptlos und sportlich mittelmässig: Der Meister von 2021 und 2022 hat in kürzester Zeit seine Glaubwürdigkeit verspielt.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: Ehemalige SP-Nationalrätin Hildegard Fässler mit 74 Jahren gestorben
KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Winterthur verbannt Smartwatches aus Klassenzimmern
nzz.description: Die neusten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: Fiasko «Reflecting Pool» in Washington: Trumps Express-Sanierung droht zu scheitern
nzz.description: Trump will das grösste Bassin auf der National Mall pünktlich zum 250. Jahrestag der Unabhängigkeitserklärung blau erstrahlen lassen. Das Projekt misslingt bis jetzt gründlich.

nzz.title: Milliardengeschenk für Iran: Die USA heben die Ölsanktionen fast ganz auf und bescheren Teheran neue Einnahmen
nzz.description: Um die Friedensgespräche zu erleichtern, darf iranisches Erdöl nahezu überall verkauft werden – sogar in die USA. Washington zeigt das grösste Entgegenkommen seit der Islamischen Revolution von 1979.

nzz.title: «Es hat eine Normalisierung der Exzesse stattgefunden», sagt der Chef von Ethos zu den Löhnen von Schweizer Topmanagern
nzz.description: Konzernchefs von SMI-Unternehmen haben letztes Jahr im Durchschnitt 8,4 Millionen Franken verdient. Das ist europäischer Spitzenwert, doch im Vergleich zu den USA bescheiden.

nzz.title: Mehr Schweizer Touristen benötigten 2025 Hilfe vom Aussendepartement
nzz.description: Wer ins Ausland reise, müsse sich im Notfall zuerst selbst helfen, erklärt das EDA pünktlich zur Ferienzeit. Zudem präsentiert das Departement konkrete Fallbeispiele von Schweizern in Notsituationen.

observador.title: UE prepara plano contra recrutamento online de menores
observador.description: Após questão da eurodeputada Ana Miguel Pedro, comissário Brunner revelou ainda processo formal aberto contra o Snapchat ao abrigo do Regulamento dos Serviços Digitais.

observador.title: França anuncia 40 mortes relacionadas com calor
observador.description: Europa enfrenta segunda onda de calor em menos de um mês. Espanha prevê 44ºC, França regista 40 mortes por afogamento e Reino Unido fecha 450 escolas.

observador.title: Há 42,6 mil exportadoras e quase 9 mil só vendem para fora
observador.description: Um estudo da Informa D&B revela o perfil das exportadoras em Portugal. O número de exportadoras cresceu, mas o perfil de exportação mudou.

observador.title: Quase 260 milhões de crianças pararam escola por conflitos
observador.description: "O número de crianças afetadas por crises aumentou 21 milhões em apenas 18 meses, atingindo um número estimado de 258 milhões em todo o mundo", afirmou o fundo Educação Não Pode Esperar.

observador.title: Incêndio em arranha-céu em Madrid deixa 4 pessoas confinadas
observador.description: A Torre Moëve, edifício de 45 andares em Madrid, foi atingida por uma explosão no 25º piso. Ainda não são conhecidas as causas do acidente.

observador.title: "O país jogou como a seleção: para o lado e para trás"
observador.description: Cristóvão Norte (PSD), Ricardo Reis (Chega) e Paulo Lopes Silva (PS) vão das críticas políticas à tática de jogo. De reparos à falta de ambição e de diálogo no país ao otimismo da vitória da seleção.

observador.title: MP pede 4 a 6 anos de prisão para Eduardo Vitor Rodrigues
observador.description: Sentença marcada para 7 de julho. Eduardo Vítor Rodrigues, que negou qualquer crime, foi acusado de lesar o erário público em mais de 15.800 euros.

observador.title: Enquanto Iraque estudou táticas, França exercitou o corpo
observador.description: França-Iraque esteve interrompido duas horas. O Iraque aproveitou para dissecar os lances do encontro, enquanto o plantel francês combateu a ansiedade do imprevisto com bicicletas estáticas.

observador.title: INEM: 6.000 chamadas extra em junho por causa do calor
observador.description: Relativamente a 2025, o INEM recebeu em junho cerca de 6.000 chamadas a mais. Este aumento está ligado às temperaturas elevadas, ao agravamento das doenças crónicas e a situações de doença aguda.

observador.title: Prisioneiros de guerra denunciam rede de recrutamento russo
observador.description: Através do Facebook e TikTok, com escalas no Brasil e Qatar, a Rússia atrai cidadãos latinos com promessas de trabalho. Três colombianos prisioneiros de guerra na Ucrânia contam como foram enganados.

observador.title: 17h. Mundial. Trump vai participar na entrega da taça
observador.description: Depois de faltar à abertura, presidente dos EUA vai marcar presença na final, assegura FIFA. Ainda neste jornal, já é conhecido o onze de Portugal frente ao Uzbequistão.

observador.title: Coindu dá início a despedimento coletivo de 48 trabalhadores
observador.description: A empresa de componentes interiores para automóveis justifica os despedimentos com a redução do uso de couro nos novos modelos previstos para 2027.

observador.title: Bar ilegal da Praia do Ourigo começa a ser demolido
observador.description: A estrutura de bar na Praia do Ourigo, no Porto, estava prevista para demolição desde 2015. Ministra questionou por que razão "uma coisa tão óbvia" exigiu processos tão complexos.

observador.title: Chips. Musk alerta Trump para risco de dependência de Taiwan
observador.description: Livro revela reunião de 2025 na Casa Branca, na qual Musk advertiu que uma invasão chinesa de Taiwan teria consequências para a economia, defendendo transferir fábricas para fora de zonas de conflito.

observador.title: Todos esperavam revolução, Martínez respondeu com evolução
observador.description: Portugal tinha uma média de 2,5 mexidas na equipa da primeira para a segunda ronda do Mundial – e nem sempre começar melhor ou pior era uma questão. Agora, Félix é a única novidade além de Rúben Dias.

observador.title: Albuquerque: há que revogar lei das finanças locais "idiota"
observador.description: O presidente do Governo da Madeira defendeu mais autonomia financeira para os municípios e criticou entidades não eleitas que "controlam os eleitos".

observador.title: JPP critica atrasos no pagamento a taxistas de doentes
observador.description: Juntos Pelo Povo apresenta projeto de resolução para pagamentos em atraso há mais de um ano aos taxistas que asseguram o transporte diário de doentes não urgentes na Madeira.

observador.title: A Europa perdeu a oportunidade de ser um ator global?
observador.description: A inação diplomática europeia perante o conflito é vista como uma falha na defesa do direito internacional. Ainda, a questão nuclear iraniana volta a dominar a agenda global.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: Portugal gegen Usbekistan im Liveticker
spiegel.description: Lionel Messi? Fünf Tore. Kylian Mbbapé? Vier Tore. Erling Haaland? Vier Tore. Cristiano Ronaldo? Null Tore. Gegen Usbekistan muss CR7 zeigen, ob er es noch drauf hat. Alles Wichtige im Livekommentar.

spiegel.title: Frankreich, Spanien, Großbritannien: Hitze macht Europa zu schaffen
spiegel.description: Höchste Warnstufen in vielen Regionen: Eine beispiellose Hitzewelle hat weite Teile Europas erfasst. Frankreich meldete die heißeste Nacht seit Beginn der Wetteraufzeichnungen – einer von vielen Rekorden.

spiegel.title: Clueso: »Ich habe kein Problem damit, ›Fuck AfD‹ zu sagen«
spiegel.description: Er wurde in der DDR geboren, lebt in Erfurt und ist einer der populärsten deutschsprachigen Musiker: Clueso. Bei »DER SPIEGEL live« auf dem Hurricane-Festival spricht er über Haltung, KI und seinen Umgang mit Nazis im Kino.

spiegel.title: Herbert Grönemeyer erhält Deutschen Nationalpreis und kritisiert deutsche Politiker
spiegel.description: Herbert Grönemeyer hat den Deutschen Nationalpreis erhalten. In seiner Dankesrede rüffelt er die deutsche Spitzenpolitik, lobt die Zivilgesellschaft und sieht sich selbst in der Verantwortung.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Rentenreform, Lehrkräfte und Politik, Trumps Probleme mit dem Reflecting Pool in Washington
spiegel.description: Die Regierung legt ein innovatives Reformpaket vor – und bremst sich dabei nicht aus. Viele Lehrkräfte wissen nicht, was sie sagen dürfen. Und Donald Trump erlebt einen grünen Albtraum. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagabend.

spiegel.title: Rente – Frührente: Gartenbauer? Altenpflegerin? Wer die »Rente mit 63« wirklich nutzt
spiegel.description: Die Rente mit 63 soll laut einem Vorschlag der Expertenkommission gestrichen werden. Welche Berufsgruppen diese Entscheidung treffen dürfte – und welche Alternativen es geben soll.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Wer Felix Nmecha zusieht, der erkennt, was Deutschland kann und was nicht
spiegel.description: Mit seiner Technik und Wucht begeistert Felix Nmecha das Publikum und ist zum heimlichen deutschen Helden der WM aufgestiegen. Er vereint, was die DFB-Elf stark macht, steht aber auch für die deutschen Schwächen.

spiegel.title: FDP: Ausschlussverfahren gegen jungen Kubicki-Fan sorgt für Unruhe
spiegel.description: Ein 17-jähriger FDP-Influencer verlässt die Jungen Liberalen – angeblich aus politischen Gründen. Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen hatte er jedoch zuvor in einer Chatgruppe rassistische und sexistische Äußerungen gepostet.

spiegel.title: Lengerich, NRW: Mann übergießt sich im Rathaus mit brennbarer Flüssigkeit
spiegel.description: Ein 47-Jähriger brachte im Rathaus von Lengerich zwei Mitarbeiter in seine Gewalt und übergoss sich mit brennbarer Flüssigkeit. Spezialkräfte der Polizei haben den Mann überwältigen können.

spiegel.title: WhatsApp: Meta ernennt indischen Unternehmer zum neuen Chef
spiegel.description: Nach sieben Jahren bekommt WhatsApp einen neuen Boss: Der Inder Kunal Shah übernimmt die Führung. Gleichzeitig investiert Meta 900 Millionen Dollar in dessen Firma.

spiegel.title: Fall Fabian: Gina H. zeigte laut Ermittlern kaum Empathie
spiegel.description: Immer wieder berichtete die Angeklagte, wie schlecht es ihr selbst gehe: Im Prozess um den getöteten Fabian ist der leitende Ermittler zu Wort gekommen. Über das Verhalten von Gina H. zeigte dieser sich erstaunt.

spiegel.title: Jordanien: Sechs Menschen hingerichtet
spiegel.description: Über Jahre wurde die Todesstrafe in Jordanien nur noch sporadisch vollstreckt. Nun hat die Justiz dort sechs Straftäter erhängt. Menschenrechtsorganisationen sind alarmiert.

spiegel.title: Tom Kaulitz äußert sich besorgt über AfD-Hoch in seiner Heimat
spiegel.description: Umfragen sehen die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt weit vorn. Tom Kaulitz findet das »besorgniserregend«. Im Interview spricht er auch darüber, wie er früher mit Punks demonstrierte und wie er heute auf seine Heimat blickt.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Parlament stimmt für Gesetzespaket zur Korruptionsbekämpfung
spiegel.description: Die EU hält wegen Korruptionsvorwürfen gegen die Orbán-Regierung Milliarden-Mittel für Ungarn zurück. Der neue Premier bekämpft diese Strukturen nun unter Hochdruck – die eingefrorenen Gelder drohen zu verfallen.

spiegel.title: Altersarmut in Ostdeutschland: Diese Rentner leben schon jetzt unterhalb der Armutsgrenze
spiegel.description: Im Osten sind immer mehr Senioren auf Sozialleistungen angewiesen. Von der Politik erwarten die Menschen nicht viel. Unser Reporter hat sich bei der Tafel in Magdeburg umgehört.

spiegel.title: Collien Fernandes - OLG Hamburg: SPIEGEL darf weiter über »virtuelle Vergewaltigung« berichten
spiegel.description: Christian Ulmen versucht, gegen den SPIEGEL-Bericht über die Vorwürfe seiner Ex-Frau Collien Fernandes vorzugehen. Nun stellt das Oberlandesgericht in Hamburg klar, dass ihre Hauptvorwürfe weiter verbreitet werden dürfen. Zwar erließ das Gericht zwei Unterlassungen, der Kern der Berichterstattung bleibt aber unberührt.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM heute: Das sollten Sie vor den Spielen am Abend und in der Nacht wissen
spiegel.description: Lässt Portugals Cristiano Ronaldo seine Kritiker mit Toren gegen Usbekistan verstummen? Luka Modrić steht vor einem Meilenstein. Und: England trifft am späten Abend auf Ghana. Das müssen Sie wissen.

phys-org.title: Attitudes, not personality, may drive deepfake pornography creation
phys-org.description: New research from Edith Cowan University (ECU) suggests attitudes, particularly those that excuse harmful behavior, may be a stronger predictor of willingness to create deepfake pornography than personality traits. phys-org.title: Although woodland salamanders have looked the same for millions of years, their physiology has evolved rapidly
phys-org.description: For her doctoral dissertation, Yale's Nathalie Alomar decided to study a small amphibian that appeared to have eluded the forces of evolution. She found that there is more to its evolution than meets the eye.

phys-org.description: Coral reef ecosystems, widely seen as a climate change bellwether, are more complex than previously understood. A new international study by the universities of Bristol, Wuhan in China, and Erlangen-Nuremberg in Germany reveals that the evolutionary advantage of coral-algae symbiosis is not fixed; it depends entirely on environmental context.

phys-org.title: Workplace structure impacts gender pay gap, study finds
phys-org.description: New Adelaide University research has identified which industries, workplace structures and employment policies are most strongly linked to gender pay gaps in Australian workplaces, with flexible work arrangements being a key indicator.

phys-org.title: Stop asking whether Pride is a protest or a party, say researchers
phys-org.description: Research examining Pride events across the U.K. has found that modern Pride celebrations have evolved into year-round community hubs that act simultaneously as protests, safe spaces and cultural festivals for local LGBTQIA+ communities.

phys-org.description: Four goose skulls were pulled from a former toilet shaft in Brandenburg, Germany, each of them riddled with strange holes. As it turns out, these holes were the telltale signs of fancy feathered crests, making them the first crested geese ever identified in the archaeological record.

phys-org.title: A new strategy can improve safety in poultry processing
phys-org.description: Salmonella is a common source of food poisoning that leads to potentially life-threatening illnesses, widespread food recalls and a consistent challenge for poultry producers. UConn Department of Animal Science associate professor Mary Anne Amalaradjou and her research team study ways to improve processing strategies to prevent foodborne illnesses by using probiotic bacteria. In a new study published in Poultry Science, they describe a method to use postbiotic compounds produced by probiotic spe

phys-org.title: Natural symbiosis: How plants and microbes share vital nutrients in fragile ecosystems
phys-org.description: Nitrogen is essential for all living organisms, but in many ecosystems it is in short supply. Plants and soil microbes both rely on nitrogen to grow, leading to intense competition below ground. Researchers at The University of Manchester have uncovered how plants and soil microbes divide up nitrogen in alpine ecosystems, helping explain how these communities coexist in nutrient limited environments. Their new study is published in Soil Biology and Biochemistry.

phys-org.title: Looking at AI startups to predict which jobs AI will affect
phys-org.description: A study of funded AI startups provides a glimpse of which jobs may be most affected by AI. As AI tools are embraced by industry after industry, the impacts of these tools on jobs remain unclear. Previous analyses have focused on the theoretical capabilities of LLMs, but social factors are also likely to play a role in shaping what aspects of work see AI integration—or full automation.

phys-org.title: Contact lenses can repair themselves with just one hour of UV light exposure
phys-org.description: Contact lenses are a great vision correction option for many, but if one of them gets damaged, there is little to do other than throw it away. A team reporting in ACS Applied Polymer Materials has a solution: special polymer hydrogels and UV light. Scratches on lenses made from their new material were easily repaired with an hour of UV light exposure. This demonstration is a first step toward the next generation of contact lenses.

phys-org.title: New method helps online ads reach overlooked groups
phys-org.description: Online advertisers and government agencies use algorithmic tools to tailor and target their campaigns to reach as many people as possible.

phys-org.title: Espresso 'pucks' stop behaving predictably above certain pressures
phys-org.description: When a physics student asked baristas at the Warsaw Coffee Conference what their biggest question for scientists was, the baristas said they wanted to know how to stop channeling during brewing.

phys-org.title: Airflow mystery solved: Heavy rain reshaped airflow through miles of underground tunnels
phys-org.description: Successfully operating in a deep underground space requires mitigating two factors: air and water.

phys-org.title: Amazon fish reveal a synchronized survival tactic that could transfer to drone swarms

phys-org.title: Study shows the good state of Garraf's fishery resources
phys-org.description: A scientific project launched by the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB) in direct collaboration with fishermen in the region has evaluated the state of fishery resources and ecological quality in the Garraf and Plana de Foix Marine Area. The species were found to be in good biological and health condition, with low levels of contaminants and an overall healthy state. The research has led to the creation of a Strategic Plan for Sustainable Fisheries.

phys-org.title: White barn owls may use moonlight to startle prey
phys-org.description: White barn owls are effective killing machines. They fly silently through the night air and swoop down on unsuspecting prey with their sharp talons. But they have something you would think goes against being a stealth predator: their white feathers. And perhaps this visual giveaway would be even worse when they glow in the moonlight.

phys-org.title: Australia's echidnas reveal a prickly scientific puzzle
phys-org.description: An echidna in Tasmania looks very different from one in Western Australia. But the differences run much deeper than appearance. A new review published in Australian Zoologist by University of Tasmania zoologist Stewart Nicol, an associate professor from the School of Natural Sciences, has found echidnas across Australia differ widely in diet, breeding, behavior and physiology, challenging long-held assumptions that they are the same.

new-sci.title: SpaceX's secretive plans to deliver cargo to Earth from space
new-sci.description: Not much is known about Starfall, SpaceX's new delivery system, but an assessment published in May revealed its intended purpose

new-sci.title: Unapproved gene therapy for boosting longevity is set to go on sale
new-sci.description: A gene therapy that instructs cells to produce more of an anti-ageing protein called klotho is about to be offered by a US company at overseas clinics to bypass FDA rules

new-sci.description: A woman with severe Alzheimer's disease who hadn't spoken more than monosyllables in years began initiating conversation after a single dose of psilocybin

new-sci.title: The surprising ways your brain changes from your 20s to your 40s
new-sci.description: When does your brain reach adulthood? We're now understanding the many ways the organ continues to mature decades after society first deems you an adult

new-sci.title: People training new AI models admit they just get chatbots to do it
new-sci.description: The next generation of AI models are meant to be trained by people paid to have conversations with them, but several of these workers have admitted to New Scientist that they simply get chatbots to do it instead. new-sci.title: We've found a mysterious substance on Titan and Pluto
new-sci.description: Something is absorbing light on the surfaces of Pluto and Saturn’s moon Titan, and figuring out what it is could be crucial to understanding Titan’s complex chemistry

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.description: Older mice that received a faecal microbiome transplant from younger animals went on to have improved brain plasticity, which suggests their brains could overcome a neurological condition that is typically successfully treated only in childhood

new-sci.title: Most portable air conditioners suck – but there's an easy fix
new-sci.description: Efficiency ratings on portable air conditioners don’t give consumers the full picture, and one type of aircon unit is so inefficient that it should be banned, says Michael Le Page

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: Gas from Uranus reveals it has an icy centre
new-sci.description: Carbon monoxide in Uranus's deep atmosphere indicates that the planet contains more ice than rock, suggesting it formed more like Neptune than we thought

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks.
